word_order: SOV | many subordinate clauses in the sample show verb-final order (e.g. "der ... gegangen war", "auf dem die Entscheidung ... beruhe"), while main clauses show verb-second patterns.
punctuation_present: always — as observed in the sample
non_boundary_traps: quotation marks around single words (e.g. „Black Box“-)
unstable_prefix_signals: fronted infinitival/PP/adverbial phrases often ending with a comma (e.g. initial "Mehr ... zu erfahren,")
subordinating conjunctions: wenn, dass, weil, obwohl, während
relative pronouns: der, die, das (introducing embedded clauses)
notes_for_prompt_writer: Prefer splitting at clause boundaries marked by commas followed by a new finite clause or by explicit subordinators, but do not finalize a segment inside subordinate (verb-final) clauses — wait for the clause-final verb. Keep trailing punctuation and closing quotes/brackets attached to the preceding segment. Avoid splitting after abbreviations (e.g. z.B.), inside hyphenated compounds, or immediately after an opening quote/parenthesis; fronted phrases followed by a comma are unstable and may require waiting for the following finite verb.
